verses.text: When Rehoboam reached Jerusalem, he gathered a hundred eighty thousand handpicked warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel and win the kingdom back for himself.
But the LORD gave this message to Shemaiah, the man of God:
"Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin.
Tell them, 'The LORD says: Don't march out to fight your own people. Everyone go home, because I brought this about.'" They listened to the LORD and turned back instead of marching against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam stayed in Jerusalem and built up the defenses of towns in Judah.
He built up Bethlehem, Etam, and Tekoa,
as well as Beth Zur, Soco, and Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, and Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, and Azekah,
and Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. These were fortified towns in Judah and Benjamin.
He strengthened the strongholds, appointed commanders, and stocked them with food, oil, and wine.
He made every town very strong and supplied it with shields and spears. Judah and Benjamin were under his rule.
The priests and Levites from every part of Israel sided with Rehoboam.
The Levites left their pasturelands and property and moved to Judah and Jerusalem. Jeroboam and his sons had barred them from serving as priests to the LORD.
Jeroboam appointed his own priests for the high places and for the goat and calf idols he had made.
After the Levites came people from every tribe of Israel who had set their hearts on seeking the LORD, the God of Israel. They came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and supported Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years. During those three years they followed the ways of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam married Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David and Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
Mahalath bore him three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
Then he married Maacah, Absalom's granddaughter. She bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Maacah, Absalom's granddaughter, more than all his other wives and concubines. He had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
Rehoboam made Maacah's son Abijah the leader among his brothers because he intended to make him king.
He acted wisely by sending some of his sons throughout Judah and Benjamin to the fortified towns. He gave them plenty of provisions and sought many wives for them.
